free_tier.stated: None. Three paid plans; the 30-day money-back guarantee is the only risk-free route.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a retrieval service, not stored bytes
per_object_cap.notes: Usenet is article-based; the object size is the poster's, not the provider's.

retention.stated: '6642+ Days' of article retention on every plan

egress.terms: 'Monthly Usenet Data Unlimited' on the Unlimited and XL plans, 50 GB on Lite. No speed cap is stated; connections are 30 on Lite and 100 on the other two.

tooling: Every usenet client: SABnzbd, NZBGet, nzbget-compatible downloaders, spotweb. No provider-side API is needed or offered.
chaining: The Unlimited plan is the feed behind a debrid or *arr stack: 100 connections and 6642 days of retention are what make an old post still downloadable, and 'Unlimited Data' is the only uncapped byte path in this whole lane.

limits.value: 50 GB/month on Lite; unlimited on Unlimited and XL
30 connections on Lite, 100 on Unlimited and XL
articles older than retention, or removed after a notice, answer 423 or 430 for that article id and the NZB cannot complete without repair data
the plan's connection count is the throughput ceiling; a client that opens more is refused at connect time

identity_cost.detail: Email and password at the signup control panel; card payment. No phone step described.

reliability_note: No incident found in the pages read. The plan page publishes 'Regularly: $19.94/mo' struck through against the $12.95 charged, which is a promotional anchor rather than a reliability matter.

evidence.proved: Lite $10.00/mo with 50 GB, Unlimited 'Regularly: $19.94/mo' struck through and '$12.95/mo' charged, XL PowerPack $15.83/mo, all with 6642+ days retention

'If your newsreader returns a "423 No Such Article" or "430 No Such Article" message ... the article may no longer be available on our servers'; retention 'adds one day ... every day' so 'no article ever expires from our servers due to time limits'.

'Retention is per provider. An article one server has aged out is very often still on another. Without a second account the only way to recover a dead article is PAR2 and that costs a read of the entire release.' Also that a second server is a second entry under the same nntp block.

notes: The charged price has not moved in 36 months; what changed is that the vendor began publishing a list price of $19.94 in 2025 that it then discounts to $12.95. The page does not say whether a renewal bills $12.95 or $19.94, and the honest reading is that $12.95 is the price as long as the promotion runs - so the exposure is 54% on renewal, not a discount a user can bank. This is the largest published promo-versus-list gap in the set after Eweka. A client that pulls older releases meets removal far more often than age. Cheapest Omicron entry seen on any of its storefronts was a 15-month promo at $1.99/mo quoted by a third-party deals page, not by the vendor, so it is not recorded as a price here.

extras.promo_gap: charged USD 12.95 against a published list of USD 19.94: the list is 54.0% higher than the charge
extras.renewal_price: not published; the page shows only the struck list price and the charged price
extras.account_states: credential refusal is 481/482/502 at connect; the page read covers article-level states only
extras.cache_miss: not applicable: an article either exists on the spool or answers 430
extras.host_removal: not applicable; the equivalent event is a backbone dropping a group or an article

interface_detail: Access is NNTP over TLS (port 563). The real interface is a standard protocol every usenet client speaks.
limits_note: The 6642-day retention figure is the vendor's own and is the same on all three plans; it is a property of the article store, not a quota.
binding_note: Lite's 50 GB/month is exhausted in under two hours at 1 TiB/month, so the plan choice is the binding decision. Unlimited removes the byte counter and leaves connection count as the only ceiling.
confidence_note: Four dated reads, three archived. The $12.95 has not moved; the strike-through list price appears only from 2025.
